title: RazorSFT: On-Policy Supervised Fine-Tuning with KL-Minimal Target Selection for Continual Learning

contributions.purpose: Mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continual LLM fine-tuning without the complexity of RL-based approaches.
contributions.mechanism: RazorSFT samples candidate responses from the current model, filters them through a task verifier, and selects the highest log-probability correct response as the SFT training target (KL-minimal selection).
contributions.evaluation: On a 3-stage continual learning benchmark, RazorSFT reduces forgetting by 60.4 percentage points vs offline SFT (FM -0.039 vs -0.643).
contributions.source_quote: We propose RazorSFT, a simple on-policy SFT method that achieves strong forgetting mitigation without the complexity of RL-based approaches.

contributions.purpose: Identify which component of on-policy training drives forgetting mitigation.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies isolating on-policy data generation from other design choices of RazorSFT.
contributions.evaluation: On-policy data accounts for 76% of the forgetting improvement over offline SFT.
contributions.source_quote: Through ablation studies, we demonstrate that on-policy data is the primary contributor to forgetting mitigation, accounting for 76% of the improvement over offline SFT.

contributions.purpose: Show a simple SFT method can match or exceed RL (GRPO) on continual learning metrics.
contributions.mechanism: Head-to-head comparison of RazorSFT against GRPO on the same 3-stage continual learning benchmark.
contributions.evaluation: RazorSFT outperforms GRPO on average accuracy (0.616 vs 0.515) and task adaptation (Countdown: 0.628 vs 0.261) with comparable forgetting mitigation.
contributions.source_quote: We show that RazorSFT outperforms GRPO on average accuracy (0.616 vs. 0.515) and task adaptation (Countdown: 0.628 vs. 0.261) while achieving comparable forgetting mitigation.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by leveraging on-policy data generation rather than explicit regularization or replay mechanisms.
Unlike these approaches, RazorSFT addresses forgetting through data selection rather than architectural constraints.

RazorSFT shares the use of on-policy data with these methods but replaces reward-based optimization with a simpler KL-minimal selection criterion, achieving comparable forgetting mitigation with reduced complexity.

RazorSFT builds on these insights by isolating the on-policy data generation mechanism from RL's reward optimization, demonstrating that simple SFT on KL-minimal on-policy targets achieves strong forgetting mitigation without the complexity of policy gradient methods.
